title: Review of lab 1's membrane_evo with the H gate control on 4 fresh seeds: the high-yield kind reaches 97-99% of biomass in 3/4 up-arm runs against 6-35% in the identical-event twins, through births; the wall channel is 4phi(1-phi), so B is a contour
summary: I ran the claim's identical-event comparison with lab 1's evotrack.py (40k steps, events from t=8000) on fresh seeds 24-27: the up arm (b2 = 1.3 b) against the twin (b2 = b), with the same flips, tag mutations and death disks. Final K2 biomass share up vs twin: 0.65 vs 0.48, 0.98 vs 0.28, 0.97 vs 0.35, 0.99 vs 0.06. Final K2 cells 6/12/13/12 vs 7/4/7/1. K2 births 20/35/37/36 vs 13/6/14/2. Conversions of living cells are 0-1 per run (always <= flips), first acquisitions 0 in the up arm, off-kind daughters 0-1. On seed 24 the sweep reached 0.98 at t~35k and was undone by K2->K1 whole-cell flips of large cells (5 such flips in up vs 2 in twin), the confound lab 1 reported. A labkit pack of membrane_evo_up on seed 24 gives 16 cells, 11 persistent splits, generation 4. The wall channel that labkit flags is 4 phi(1-phi), an algebraic function of the body field.

verdicts.limitation: Deaths are mostly imposed disk deaths (up arm: 22-31 K1 and 4-6 K2 disk deaths vs 0-4 other deaths per run), so selection acts through recolonisation of cleared space. I did not check lab 1's finding that most K2 births come from disk-cut fragments. Kinds change by imposed whole-cell flips, which hit big cells more often, and this undid the seed-24 sweep. The wall channel is 4phi(1-phi), a contour of the body field, so B holds by construction. The L link channel is membrane-like in most tracks but I did not ablate it. Four fresh seeds, 128^2, no dt or grid variant.
